definitions.explanation: A sweet Japanese rice wine used as a seasoning in cooking to add mild sweetness and shine to dishes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{味醂|みりん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{加|くわ}える→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧。

examples.english: Adding mirin gives the dish a nice glaze.
examples.notes: 照りが出る refers to the glossy appearance mirin creates

examples.japanese: ⟦{煮物|にもの}→煮物：04971_nimono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{味醂|みりん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{欠|か}かせない→欠かせない：24096_kakasenai⟧。
examples.english: Mirin is essential for simmered dishes.

examples.english: Mixing equal amounts of soy sauce, mirin, and sake makes a versatile sauce for simmered dishes.

notes:
A fundamental seasoning in Japanese cooking along with soy sauce and sake. Types include:
- ⟦{本|ほん}みりん→本みりん：28722_honmirin⟧ (true mirin, contains alcohol)
- みりん⟦{風|ふう}→風：noentry⟧⟦{調味料|ちょうみりょう}→調味料：04941_choumiryou⟧ (mirin-like seasoning, low/no alcohol)

Common uses:
- Adds sweetness and depth to sauces
- Creates ⟦{照|て}り→照り：16401_teri⟧ (glaze) on grilled foods
- Reduces fishy odors in seafood dishes
- Part of the classic ⟦{割|わ}り{下|した}→割り下：10039_warishita⟧ (sukiyaki sauce) ratio
